scams.name: The Nara Park Deer Antler & Bite Injury
scams.description: Visitors purchase shika senbei crackers near Todai-ji and become surrounded by wild deer that bite, nip, and occasionally inflict antler wounds. The Nara Prefectural Government documented 159 injury cases in fiscal 2024, with 111 involving tourists. September–October mating season sees heightened aggression, with September 2024 alone producing 35 injuries and 10 hospitalizations—a sevenfold increase year-over-year.
scams.avoidance: Purchase and distribute one pack of crackers quickly rather than teasing. Keep hands raised and empty when out of food. Avoid stags with full antlers August–November. Never allow children to feed deer unattended. Read multilingual warning pamphlets. Wash any bite wounds with tap water and contact the Nara Deer Preservation Foundation at +81-742-22-2388 for serious injuries.
scams.location: Nara Park, Todai-ji approach, Kasuga Taisha approach

scams.name: The Sanjo-dori / Higashimuki-dori Souvenir Shakedown
scams.description: Generic souvenir shops along the approach to Todai-ji charge 2–3 times department-store prices for keychains, fans, and cakes. More significantly, shopkeepers exhibit rude behavior toward foreign tourists, including shouting and spraying water at visitors lingering outside storefronts. Multiple Google Maps reviews document dismissive treatment and forced exits.
scams.avoidance: Skip Sanjo-dori and Higashimuki-dori strips; purchase identical items at Don Quijote or Kintetsu Nara department store for 30–50% savings. Visit branded craft specialists instead of generic souvenir shops. Avoid bus-tour captive venues. Check Google Maps ratings—anything under 3.8★ is a reliable warning sign. Report aggressive behavior to Nara's Tourist Information Center at Kintetsu Nara Station 2F.
scams.location: Sanjo-dori shopping street, Higashimuki-dori, Todai-ji Nanmon approach

scams.name: The Nara Ryokan Bait-and-Switch
scams.description: Guests book traditional ryokan accommodations based on appealing photos but experience room downgrades upon arrival with vague justifications. Properties like Wakasa Bettei and Hotel New Wakasa have clustered complaints describing "おとり広告" (bait-and-switch advertising). Issues include switched rooms, non-functional outdoor baths, double-billing disputes, and refusal to process cancellations or refunds.
scams.avoidance: Book only properties with 50+ English reviews and 4.2+ ratings, weighing recent reviews heavily. Screenshot exact room and amenity photos before booking. Photograph check-in bills. Obtain written email confirmation of all cancellations—automated replies alone are insufficient. Avoid double-booking across platforms. Prefer Japan Ryokan Association-certified properties or established chains. Report fraud immediately to Booking.com, Rakuten Travel, or Jalan.
scams.location: Nara city hotels near Kintetsu Nara Station and Todai-ji

scams.name: The Nara Taxi Long-Route Detour
scams.description: Taxi drivers take unnecessarily long routes to inflate fares, such as routing a 2 km trip via prefectural roads to create a 6.8 km detour. Drivers may ask passengers to confirm route names rather than entering destinations into GPS. Nara Kintetsu Taxi (2.5★ / 62 reviews) and sister company Kai-Nara Taxi (1.9–2.0★) both display clustered complaints about meter-running and rude behavior.
scams.avoidance: Use the GO taxi app for Nara Kintetsu Taxi—it displays routes and fares before boarding. Show drivers Google Maps with highlighted routes and decline verbal alternatives. Walk distances under 2 km (Kintetsu Nara Station to Todai-ji is ~20 minutes). Use the Nara City Loop Bus or rail for station transfers. Prefer higher-rated stands: 近鉄奈良駅前観光タクシー乗り場 (4.0★) or 近鉄奈良駅前中型タクシー乗り場 (5.0★). Only use green-plate licensed taxis.
scams.location: Kintetsu Nara Station / JR Nara Station taxi stands
